hints: Look carefully at position P in the Venn diagram. It sits in the middle where all three circles overlap, so what three features must a tube have at once?
Think down the airway from trachea to bronchus to bronchiole. Which one loses its cartilage support and its mucus-secreting goblet cells first?
walkthrough:
**Decode what P means**

Hello, let us read the diagram together. P is the central overlap of all three circles.

So any tube at P must have all three features at the same time: ciliated epithelium AND goblet cells AND cartilage.

**Recall the structure of each airway**

The trachea has C-shaped cartilage rings to hold it open, plus a ciliated epithelium with goblet cells for the mucus escalator. The bronchus is very similar, it still has cartilage plates, ciliated epithelium and goblet cells.

The bronchiole is much narrower. It keeps some ciliated epithelium and smooth muscle, but it has no cartilage and no goblet cells.

**Match to the table**

So bronchus = yes, trachea = yes, bronchiole = no.

That combination is bronchus tick, bronchiole cross, trachea tick, which is option C.

options.A: Incorrect because bronchiole cannot be at P. It lacks cartilage and goblet cells, so it does not have all three features.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes bronchiole and excludes trachea. The trachea definitely has all three features and the bronchiole does not.
options.C: Correct because both bronchus and trachea have ciliated epithelium, goblet cells and cartilage, while bronchiole has neither cartilage nor goblet cells.
options.D: Incorrect because it excludes bronchus and includes bronchiole. The bronchus has all three features, the bronchiole does not.
